title: Degenerated PCR with GoTaq Hot Start
author: Eduardo Dupim
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.szyef7w
materials: Degenerated PCR Program: Differently of the normal PCR thermocycler programs, the degenerated PCR have more time for annealing. xºC = optimal annealing temperature for the pair of primers.

We used different thermocyle programs, according to the primers. In all programs, the GoTaq Hot Start Polymerase was previous incubated for 2 minutes to be activated. The PCRs were performed in a Applied Biosystems Veriti™ 96-Well Thermal Cycler (Cat#4375786). 1) Degenerated PCR Program: Differently of the normal PCR thermocycler programs, the degenerated PCR have more time for annealing. xºC = optimal annealing temperature for the pair of primers. 2) Degenerated Touchdown PCR (TD-PCR) Program: In TD-PCR, we screen a range of annealing temperatures to try optimize the reaction in different species samples. So, we have a stage where the annealing temperature decrease -0.2ºC by cycle, in the end of this stage, the annealing temperature decreased -4ºC. xºC = optimal annealing temperature for the pair of primers. References: Sambrook, J. & Russell, D. W. (2001) 'Chapter 8. Protocol 11. Mixed Oligonucleotide-primed Amplification of cDNA' in Molecular cloning : a laboratory manual. Cold Spring Harbor: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, p. 8.66-8.71.

steps.title: Prepare master mix
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to make a master mix for 1,000 reactions (total volume 18 mL): 11.6 mL DEPC‑treated water, 4.0 mL 5× Green GoTaq Flexi Buffer, 2.0 mL 25 mM MgCl₂, and 0.4 mL 10 mM dNTP mix. Mix gently until homogeneous.

steps.title: Aliquot and store mix
steps.instruction: Dispense the master mix into 1 mL aliquots, label each tube, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Add DNA template
steps.instruction: When setting up each PCR, use a DNA template at a concentration of at least 10 µg/µL.
